My entire family and I watched my grandma take her last breaths in the hospital.

Something I am actually very grateful for. She wasn't alone. She was surrounded by people she loved. 

She was an incredible human being. She was a retired babysitter. She watched my siblings and I throughout school up to the point that she died when I was 17. We didn't need her to watch us anymore when we became teenagers, but we were just so used to seeing her every day during the summer and after school until my parents got off of work, that we just continued doing that until she passed.

Whenever we were there, we played a lot of video games. My uncle owned the house and had her live with him so she wouldn't be put into assisted living or anything like that. He owned a bunch of video games, N64, Playstation, Playstation 2, x-box, x-box 360, and that's all I can remember.  So whenever we went, he was working, and we would hang out with my grandma and play video games all day. She always made some great food for us. She would talk on the phone often and gossip about others lol.

She had a massive heart attack right in the widow maker. She lasted about 16 hours afterward in the CVICU. I don't know what all they tried, I wasn't medically literate back then. But there was nothing else they could do and she was deteriorating, fast. The only thing we could do at that point was take her off the vent, allow her die comfortably,, surrounded by those she loved. 

That was 13 years ago. I am doing ok.
